_meta.purpose: Small curated knowledge base. The model may only cite entries from this file, by id. Section numbers are shown to the model and to users ONLY when 'section' is set (i.e. checked). Entries whose section number is unchecked keep it in 'section_pending' and the system never reveals it.

verification_levels.verified: Bare-act text seen during the build on a third-party legal site (see verified_via); the official India Code page has not yet been opened.
verification_levels.secondary_verified: Confirmed in two or more reputable secondary sources (law firm / legal news); official India Code page still to be opened before production use.
verification_levels.single_secondary: Seen in one secondary source only. Treat as provisional.
verification_levels.general_principle: Widely accepted general position, no specific provision claimed. No section is cited.
verification_levels.pending_section: The instrument exists but the specific section number has NOT been checked. No section is cited.

_meta.reviewer_note: Before any real deployment, a qualified Indian advocate must review every entry and the official links must be opened and confirmed.

entries.act: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021
entries.title: Which consumer commission hears the complaint
entries.summary: Consumer disputes are heard by a three-tier system. Under the 2021 Rules the tier depends on the value of the goods or services paid as consideration: District Commission up to Rs 50 lakh, State Commission above Rs 50 lakh up to Rs 2 crore, National Commission above Rs 2 crore.
entries.jurisdiction_note: Territorial rules decide which District Commission; confirm with the commission or an advocate.

entries.title: Two-year limitation for a consumer complaint
entries.summary: A complaint must be filed within two years from the date the cause of action arose. A commission may admit a late complaint only if it is satisfied there was sufficient cause for the delay and records its reasons.
verified_via: bare-act text of Section 69(1) seen on advocatekhoj.com
second secondary source confirming the delay-condonation proviso

entries.title: What a commission can order
entries.summary: If a complaint about defective goods, deficient service or an unfair trade practice is proved, a commission can order remedies such as removal of the defect, replacement, refund of the price paid, and compensation. Whether and how much is decided case by case.

entries.title: Who is a consumer; defects, deficiency and unfair trade practices
entries.summary: The Act protects a person who buys goods or hires services for consideration, other than for resale or a commercial purpose. It deals with defective goods, deficiency in service and unfair trade practices, including online sales.
entries.jurisdiction_note: Purchases made for a business or resale may fall outside the definition; an advocate should check.

entries.title: Rules for online marketplaces and sellers
entries.summary: These rules put duties on e-commerce entities, including having a grievance officer and handling complaints within a set time. The exact duties and time limits must be checked in the Rules text before relying on them.
entries.jurisdiction_note: Applies to e-commerce entities covered by the Rules.

entries.act: National Consumer Helpline (Department of Consumer Affairs)
entries.title: National Consumer Helpline: a free pre-litigation step
entries.summary: The Department of Consumer Affairs runs the National Consumer Helpline, where a consumer can register a grievance against a seller or company before going to a commission. Contact options (portal, phone, app) should be confirmed on the official site.
entries.jurisdiction_note: Not a court; outcomes depend on the company's response.

entries.title: Filing a consumer complaint online
entries.summary: Consumer complaints can be filed online through the consumer commissions' e-filing portal (e-Daakhil, which one source reports now runs at e-jagriti.gov.in). Portal names and fee slabs change, so confirm on the Department of Consumer Affairs website. One source reports no fee for claims up to Rs 5 lakh.
entries.jurisdiction_note: Portal availability can vary by state commission.

entries.title: Wage laws changed in November 2025: Payment of Wages Act is repealed
entries.summary: The Code on Wages, 2019 came into force generally on 21 November 2025 (Notification S.O. 5322(E)). Its Section 69 repealed the Payment of Wages Act 1936, the Minimum Wages Act 1948, the Payment of Bonus Act 1965 and the Equal Remuneration Act 1976. Salary disputes arising now are therefore dealt with under the Code, not the old Acts. Central Rules followed in May 2026; state rules are at different stages.
entries.jurisdiction_note: State rules differ in readiness. Whether the Code covers a particular worker depends on whether they are an 'employee' as defined; an advocate or labour office should confirm.

entries.title: Time limit for paying wages, including on leaving a job
entries.summary: Section 17 sets time limits for payment of wages by wage period. Law-firm summaries also report that when an employee is removed, dismissed, retrenched or resigns, wages are due within two days. Read the exact wording of Section 17 and the applicable state rules before quoting the timeline.
entries.jurisdiction_note: Exact periods and any state-specific rules should be confirmed.

entries.title: Time limit for claiming unpaid wages
entries.summary: Secondary sources report that claims for unpaid wages and other dues under the Code can be made within three years, longer than the twelve months under the repealed Payment of Wages Act. The Section 45 wording and how it applies to the claimant should be checked.
verified_via: factohr.com note citing Section 45 for claims
entries.jurisdiction_note: Provisional. Confirm before relying on any deadline.

entries.title: Deductions from wages
entries.summary: The Code permits only certain deductions from wages and limits them. An employer cannot deduct arbitrarily. Which deductions are lawful must be checked against the Code and the employment contract.
entries.jurisdiction_note: An advocate or labour office should check the specific deduction.

entries.act: State labour department / authority under the Code on Wages, 2019
entries.title: Where an unpaid salary complaint goes
entries.summary: Unpaid wage claims are generally taken to the labour authority of the state where the workplace is. The correct office, forms and online options differ by state and must be checked with the state labour department. A written demand to the employer is a usual first step.
entries.jurisdiction_note: State-specific. Do not assume the office or form.

entries.act: Rental agreement and state rent law
entries.title: The agreement and your state's rent law decide the deposit rules
entries.summary: India has no single central rule that fixes when a security deposit must be returned. The terms of the written (or proven oral) rental agreement and the rent law of your state generally govern deductions and timing. Reading the agreement's deposit, notice-period and damage clauses is the first step.
entries.jurisdiction_note: State-specific. Ask the user's state and city.

entries.title: Model Tenancy Act is a template that states must adopt
entries.summary: The Model Tenancy Act, 2021 was issued by the Centre as a model for states. It applies in a state only if that state has adopted it or enacted a similar law. Check whether the user's state has done so before describing any rights from it.
entries.jurisdiction_note: Adoption varies by state; unverified for the user's state.

entries.act: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908; Limitation Act, 1963
entries.title: Civil suit to recover a withheld deposit
entries.summary: A tenant can usually sue in a civil court to recover money that is owed. A written agreement may allow a faster summary procedure in some courts. Money claims generally have a limitation period (commonly three years from when the right to sue arose), but the starting date and the right procedure depend on the facts, so an advocate should confirm.
entries.jurisdiction_note: Court, procedure and limitation start date need an advocate's confirmation.

entries.title: A written demand notice is customary before suing
entries.summary: A written demand (legal notice) with a reasonable deadline is the usual step before filing a case. It documents the dispute and shows good faith. In ordinary private disputes it is generally not itself a legal requirement, although a court may look at whether a demand was made.
entries.jurisdiction_note: Special rules apply if the other party is a government body.

entries.act: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 (NALSA and State/District Legal Services Authorities)
entries.title: Free legal aid, Lok Adalat and mediation
entries.summary: National, State and District Legal Services Authorities provide free legal services to eligible persons, and Lok Adalats help settle disputes by agreement. Eligibility categories apply; check with the District Legal Services Authority or NALSA.
entries.jurisdiction_note: Eligibility and process vary; confirm with the local authority.

entries.title: Check a case or notice on eCourts
entries.summary: eCourts services let a person look up case status and listed dates for many courts using case details. It can help confirm whether a notice or case is genuine, but a lawyer should read the notice itself.
